clauses.mechanism: express revocation of EO 7165 performed by this order itself on November 18, 1947 (effective upon filing for publication, which occurred that day)
clauses.reason: The sole clause orders Executive Order 7165 of August 29, 1935 revoked and adds the sentence "This order shall become effective upon" its filing for publication in the Federal Register. The filing line reads "Filed, Nov. 18, 1947;" and the signature date is "November 18, 1947.", so the revocation took effect, and the command to revoke was performed and exhausted, on November 18, 1947. The first-end source is the held Federal Register text of the order itself. No later instrument, amendment, extension or earlier event alters or ends the command: the dossier chain is empty and the order states no until-date, report date or condition.

research_rationale:
EO 9906 was read in full in the registered Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9906.txt, 12 FR 7799, PDF page 1); the census register row (date, title, President) agrees with the heading, title and date line printed in that text. The order's one operative sentence revokes Executive Order 7165 of August 29, 1935. Page location was checked against the PDF page markers of the held text layer only; no page image was inspected. The representation is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, held as original_representation_unverified. The sentence "This order shall become effective upon" its filing for publication fixes the date by the filing line, which reads "Filed, Nov. 18, 1947;"; the signature date is "November 18, 1947." as well, so the revocation took effect on November 18, 1947. Under owner ruling 2026-10-28 (evidence decides) a command that was performed on its date is recorded as exhausted by performance on that date.

savings.reason: The order contains no savings, transfer or residual clause; it only revokes Executive Order 7165. The machine searches of the U.S. Code and the eCFR (both as of the October 14, 2026 cutoff, edition caveats stated in their coverage notes) and the Federal Register catalog return no hit citing EO 9906, so no held source continues any command of this order.
